text:
samir: heads-up — saw a ~2x p95 latency spike on runtime-serving v2 at 03:07 UTC, throughput dipped too. KV cache miss_rate jumped from ~3% -> ~28% on shard gpu-09. Traces for those requests are missing in honeycomb (sampling? scraper gap?).
elaine: looking. are these user-facing errors or just latency? any 5xx?
samir: no 5xx, just latency. dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/serving/runtime?panelId=kernel-metrics shows miss rate and p95.
alex_w: seeing a noisy neighbor event on gpu-09 earlier, might be preemptible job causing context switches. kernel-select logs show fallback to generic kernels around that time.
maria: can you paste the kernel logs? want to check exact timestamps and trace alignment.
samir: pasted logs:
```\n[03:06:58] kernel-select: model=redwood-1b arch=attn_v2 selected=fast_matmul
[03:07:01] kernel-select: model=redwood-1b arch=attn_v2 selected=generic_matmul (fallback)
[03:07:05] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.279 active_keys=124k host=gpu-09
```\nelaine: that's odd — fallback should have trace_id attached. honeycomb shows a gap 03:06:59-03:07:08 for gpu-09. sampling config might have been overridden by opsbot during a previous incident.
alerts-bot: Incident #INC-2025-289 created: runtime-p95-spike; paging eng-sre.
alex_w: can we repro locally? maybe perf regression in kernel selection heuristics from last week's change.
maria: release notes mention "improve kernel selection for long token lengths" — could be heuristic edge-case. @samir can you run the profiler dump from the affected pod?
samir: running now, profiler output:
```\ncpu: 14% -> 60% at 03:07
kv_cache_lookup: latency p95 12ms -> 48ms
batcher: build_latency p99 9ms -> 120ms
```\nelaine: batcher spike suggests batching heuristics didn't collapse requests properly — combined with KV misses multiplies token gen time.
alex_w: also see our metrics backend had a scrapers gap for that cluster at 03:06:50-03:07:20, prometheus logs show `write: timeout` — explains missing metrics/traces, but kernel logs from hosts still present.
maria: ops: can you check node-level dmesg / kube events for GPU context switches or preemptions? maybe noisy neighbor eviction.
opsbot: checked node gpu-09: container preemption events at 03:06:59 and 03:07:03, source=batch-internal.
samir: ok that matches. hypothesized chain: noisy neighbor preemption -> kernel fallback (slower kernels) + KV cache churn -> batching stalls -> p95 spike. observability gap due to metrics scraper timeouts and reduced trace sampling.
elaine: action items:
- patch: revert heuristic commit a1b2c3 if we can reproduce (alex_w)
- fix: increase tracer sampling and attempt trace backfill where possible (maria)
- infra: investigate why prometheus writes timed out and harden scrapers (ops)
- longer term: improve batching resilience to KV cache churn and add circuit-breaker for fallback kernels (runtime team)
alex_w: quick win: attach `trace_id` and `pod_id` to kernel-select and kv_cache logs so we can correlate without full traces.
samir: agreed. I'll open tickets and attach profiler dumps + log snippets.
maria: thanks all — let's regroup in 30m if we have repro.
samir: thx all :thumbsup:
